This is sand leveling, or topdressing. It creates a more level surface for your lawn by filling in low areas. I use masonry sand since I have Bermuda grass. If you have a cool season grass type, a screened topsoil may be better. I like to put a little fertilizer down prior to, and after to ensure bermuda is growing aggressively through the sand. I wanted to give this plain front yard a premium upgrade, so I grabbed my tools and got to work! Watching the real progress unfold in this timelapse is incredibly satisfying. Here is a step-by-step breakdown of how I built this modern rock garden: 1️⃣ First, I mapped out a smooth, curved border on the grass using white spray paint. 2️⃣ Next, I dug out the edge along the line and laid down a heavy-duty black weed barrier. 3️⃣ I installed a sleek stone border, block by block, to keep everything neat and contained. 4️⃣ Then came the best part—pouring and leveling tons of crisp white river rocks for that beautiful, high-contrast look. 5️⃣ Finally, I styled the space by placing a dark statement sphere, planting some architectural agaves, and adding solar pathway lights. Seeing the before and after of this build progress makes all the hard work totally worth it! ✨ Want a stunning, weed-free flower bed? Try this easy "pot-in-pot" landscaping hack to keep your borders looking fresh all year long! 📦 First, lay down cardboard along your path and space out heavy-duty black base pots on top. The cardboard acts as an amazing, natural weed barrier. 💧 Next, pour gravel all around the base pots. This hides the cardboard, holds your base pots securely in place, and provides excellent water drainage. 🪴 Now just drop your decorative plants-still in their own nursery pots-directly into the base pots! You can swap them out in seconds when seasons change or easily lift them inside if a freeze hits. 💡 Pro-tips: Mix up your flower colors, put the taller plants in the back, and always match your plants to the amount of sunlight that wall gets.

This company is turning landfills back into landscapes Zigma Global clears landfill waste and reclaims old dump yards in India using a scientific process called bio-mining. Government estimates that there are 2,424 dump yard sites in India, holding close to 16 crore tonnes of legacy waste across roughly 15,000 acres. Most of it is land that sits on the city and surrounded by neighbourhoods. The old fix was capping which was to cover the mound with soil. It’s cheaper, but the waste underneath keeps producing methane and leachate, and the land stays dead. Zigma has collaborated with Singapore headquartered waste management corporation Blue Planet Environmental Solutions. Waste is excavated and processed to separate materials such as recyclables, organic matter, inert material and Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF). The RDF can then be used as an alternative fuel in industries such as cement manufacturing, where suitable facilities are equipped to use it. The other fractions have their own routes. Recovered soil goes into landscaping and levelling low-lying land and recyclables re-enter the material stream. What’s left at the end is land. Sites that sat for decades leaching into groundwater, catching fire in summer, emitting methane now becomes an open ground that cities can actually use again.
